clue.text: Conceding why bride-to-be is with dressmaker reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the phrase is judged by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: she visits the dressmaker 'for fitting' of her wedding dress

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a bride-to-be is spending time at the dressmaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'for fitting' answers the question and, said quickly, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit something is to give it up or surrender it, so conceding is a fair present-participle synonym.

clue.text: Agree in acting together to withhold payment

indicators.note: to withhold means to keep back, so these letters are kept out of the longer word

parts.note: things that are concurrent happen or act together
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: Agreeing to act jointly in refusing to pay, like tenants on a rent strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withhold' takes RENT out of CONCURRENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Native American, one miles adrift

indicators.note: something adrift is loose and out of place, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A Native American traveller who has wandered a mile off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges ONE MILES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seminole are a Native American people of Florida and Oklahoma.

clue.text: Drunkard from Kent area acquiring bad smell

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
pong is British slang for a stink

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker from Kent who has started to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; 'acquiring' signals that the smell goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is informally a heavy drinker, one who soaks up alcohol.

clue.text: Possesses items second husband dropped in battle

parts.note: possesses means has

indicators.note: second picks out which of the two letters in the run is to go: the one in the following word
dropped means let fall away, so this letter is removed

parts.note: items are things

explanation.surface: Someone owns items that a second husband let fall during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' marks which H goes: once HAS is in place, the H of the following word is the second one in the run, and 'dropped' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 was where William the Conqueror defeated Harold.

clue.text: Pack Stuart's case with pained expression

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the outer letters of the name are used

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Packing Stuart's suitcase while wincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outer letters ST of Stuart.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or store away neatly.

clue.text: Couple book absorbing week overseas on vacation

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A couple book a week's holiday abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' keeps only the outside of overseas; 'absorbing' says the book holds the week and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, which is a couple.

clue.text: Resort hotelier's lost cat

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside hotelier has lost their cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like the seaside town but is re-sort, rearranging HOTELIER'S LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with a mottled black, orange and cream coat.

clue.text: Photo captures ultimate source of environmental pollution

indicators.note: captures means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
ultimate means last

explanation.surface: A photograph that shows the root cause of environmental damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded polymer packaging is a notorious cause of litter in oceans and landscapes.

clue.text: Type of ball towards winger, hotshot in football team

parts.note: a crystal ball is what a fortune teller gazes into
winger is Royal Navy slang for a friend or chum
an ace is an expert, a hotshot

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a ball sent out to the winger, with the star player in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: CRYSTAL PALACE is a London football club. 'Type of ball' wants to be a football pass; it is a fortune teller's crystal ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is a professional English club side based in south London.

clue.text: Thought student is going for meal

indicators.note: is going means leaving, so this letter is removed

parts.note: reflection is careful thought
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student muses about going for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is going' removes L from REFLECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Refection is an old word for a light meal or refreshment.

clue.text: Brownish-coloured river visited by swans regularly

indicators.note: visited by means having something come inside, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brown river where swans come by now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes W and N from swans; 'visited by' puts them inside TAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny describes an orange-brown or yellowish-brown colour, as of a lion's coat.

clue.text: Woven material provided from the East? That is right

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the East means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: so can mean provided that

explanation.surface: A query about whether some woven fabric came from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets.

clue.text: During hours of darkness, mistake having change of heart

indicators.note: the heart, the central letter, is swapped for another

parts.note: an oversight is an error made by not noticing

explanation.surface: Someone makes an error overnight and then changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' swaps the middle S of OVERSIGHT for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight means through the night, while it is dark.

clue.text: Creature adapting easily to eat half of peeled banana

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so the piece goes inside
easily here signals the word is loosely rearranged
half of takes the first half of what remains
peeled means skin removed, so the outer letters go

explanation.surface: A creature that adapts readily to eating part of a banana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapting' looks like the creature's behaviour but is the fodder, scrambled by 'easily' to GIANTPDA; 'peeled' and 'half of' work on banana, and 'to eat' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a bear native to China, famous for eating bamboo.

clue.text: Various English beaches may be covered with it

definitions.text: beaches may be covered with it

indicators.note: various means of different kinds, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A remark on what covers many of England's beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges ENGLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, common on English shores.

clue.text: Relative number extremely shocked, near rage occasionally, is rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up, backwards
extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters
occasionally means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A shocked relative's anger flares up now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SD, 'occasionally' gives NARG, and 'is rising' reverses NOSDNARG.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a family member, a child's son.

clue.text: This month everything will be set up

parts.note: inst., instant, is old business-letter shorthand for this month
all means everything

explanation.surface: An announcement that everything will be in place this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for instant, meant 'of this month' in formal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment is to set it up ready for use.

clue.text: Romantic dates I arranged, embracing Liz endlessly

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the trimmed name goes in
arranged means put in order, so these letters are rearranged
endlessly means without its last letter

explanation.surface: A romantic sets up dates and hugs Liz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DATES I; 'endlessly' trims Liz to LI, which 'embracing' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist, like a romantic, pursues lofty dreams over practical reality.

clue.text: Leaving hotel, star in huge Rolls giving autograph

indicators.note: rolls means tumbles, so the remaining letters are mixed
leaving means departing, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A star leaves the hotel in a huge Rolls-Royce, signing autographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' removes H from STAR IN HUGE; 'Rolls' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's name written by hand, as an autograph is.

clue.text: Individual supporting a French duke's tip is ruined

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed beneath

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A single person holding up a French duke ends up ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ONE below UN and D in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone is an old-fashioned way to say brought to ruin.

clue.text: Round flatbread? That's mine, thanks!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone claims a round flatbread as theirs, with thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like 'belongs to me' but is a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, round Middle Eastern bread that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Flexible recruitment essentially in factory

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the other word

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A factory with a flexible hiring policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives I, the middle of recruitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means bending easily, supple.

clue.text: Made faux pas picked up in London's East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of East London drop their H, so the word is said without it

parts.note: picked up means heard

explanation.surface: Social blunders overheard in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Cockney (East End London) accent HEARD loses its H and becomes 'EARD, which matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a faux pas is a social slip, so to make one is to have erred.

clue.text: Value degree

definitions.meaning: to value is to assess or rank something
a degree of speed or progress, as in at a fast pace

explanation.definitionFit: Rate means both to appraise something and a measure of speed or extent.

clue.text: Spiritual leader from Koutiala, Mali, a lady upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spiritual leader turns up from a town in Mali; a lady is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'from' is that indicator, so it is now named on the hidden-word step.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Disappointment in state of one's car tyres, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a disappointment is something that fails to meet expectations

definitions.text: state of one's car tyres, perhaps
definitions.meaning: tyres with the air released are flat, deflated

explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is an anticlimax; tyres that have been let down are deflated.

clue.text: Pop off after function for an indefinite period

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
pop off is slang for die

explanation.surface: Someone dies after some ceremony, gone for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Sine die is Latin, 'without a day', used of adjournments with no date set.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjourned sine die means postponed with no date fixed, indefinitely.
